items.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995…
items.q: And the finale we usually choose a composer that’s usually Ellington and sometimes it’s just standards... everybody will play one or maybe two choruses of their favorite by that composer.

ctx.x: How many of you play at once?

Never more than two at a time. They have one bass player and one drummer. Bob Cranshaw is the bass player and Alan Dawson usually is the drummer but he was put in the hospital shortly before we left, I think he’s going to be all right though, and Grady Tate made it this year. And the way they do it, you know like six guys will play alone, I mean, each one of them will play alone for about twelve or fifteen minutes with the rhythm section, which usually makes up about two tunes. And then there’s an © Fillius Jazz…

intermission. Then the other four. There are two piano duets with or without the rhythm section at their own desire, whatever they want to do. And it changes up every night. The next night there is a different six in the front and a different four and it goes on like that. And the finale we usually choose a composer that’s usually Ellington and sometimes it’s just standards, you know, well-known standards, and everybody will play one or maybe two choruses of their favorite by that composer.
